verdict.headline: Stocks close at records as oil slumps on Iran talks and AI spending thesis holds
verdict.label: BUY — SPX 7,737 (ATH, +1.79%); Dow 54,086 (record, +1.71%); Nasdaq 26,585 (+2.59%); PLTR $158.81 (+26.4%); AVGO $420.12 (+7.1%); AMD AH −8% to ~$477 on $6.7B data-center beat; SPCX $125.33 close, AH −8.6% to $114.60 on capex concern; WTI $76.14 (−5.2%); September hike 54%; 30Y 5.20% sole breach; 1-of-6 regime
verdict.rationale_short: Every regime condition the morning outlined as the bull case materialized: SPX set a new all-time record, oil cleared the $79 threshold, September hike fell to 54% on cooling JOLTS. The AI spending thesis held across the regular session — PLTR's Monday AH beat carried +26.4% into the close, AVGO surged 7.1% on a $128.1B purchase commitment, and AMD confirmed $6.7B in data-center revenue (+107% YoY). The AH tape told a different story: AMD fell ~8% and SPCX fell 8.6% to $114.60 despite beating revenue estimates by 12.7%, confirming that AI infrastructure plays are fully priced at elevated pre-earnings entries and the tape is selling strength, not rewarding it. One breach remains: the 30Y at 5.20%, 20bps above the 5.00% clearing threshold. Oil deflation has front-loaded its rate-relief contribution; NFP Friday (consensus +91K) is the first real data test of the path to closure.

Monday's structural shift — commercial grew faster than government — is now the baseline; any Q3 commercial deceleration below 100% at this multiple compresses the stock materially.

trade_setups.thesis: AMD printed $11.54B revenue (+50%) and $6.7B data-center revenue (+107%) then sold off 8% after hours. The morning was precise: AMD had risen from $484 to $518.58 before reporting, compressing the margin such that even a strong $6.7B data-center result repriced as a sell-the-news event. The setup now is a post-selloff stabilization test: does $477 (AH settlement) hold after the premium fully unwinds, or does the regular session continue the retracement toward the pre-PLTR-read-through range of $440-450? The $484 Monday close is the anchor; two consecutive closes below it signal the PLTR premium has fully reverted.
trade_setups.entry: $518.58 (Aug 4 close before AH); $484 (Monday close, pre-PLTR premium); $477 AH settlement; $440-450 pre-read-through range.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close back above $518 signals buyers absorbed the AH selloff; a close below $440 signals full PLTR premium retracement.

trade_setups.asset: 30Y yield — path to 5.00% through data sequence
trade_setups.thesis: The 30Y at 5.20% is the sole remaining regime breach, 20bps above the 5.00% clearing threshold. Oil deflation has front-loaded its contribution over three sessions (~−8bps total). Closing the remaining 20bps requires labor and inflation data. NFP Friday below 80K pushes September well below 50%, giving the 30Y a technical path toward 5.00%. CPI August 13 below 3.0% would extend it. September at 54% is already 16 points below the 70% trigger; NFP and CPI determine whether that gap widens or narrows.
trade_setups.entry: 5.00% is the formal clearing level. NFP August 7 and CPI August 13 are the two data points that determine the path.
trade_setups.invalidation: NFP above 130K restores September above 70%, sends 30Y back toward 5.28%, and re-triggers the formal breach.
trade_setups.horizon: 1-3 weeks; NFP August 7 and CPI August 13 are the key dates

trade_setups.thesis: SpaceX's first public earnings showed $7.81B revenue (+92% YoY) beating estimates by 12.7%, with AI segment growing 247% YoY to $2.6B. But capex of $18.37B ($15.83B in AI) represents a 2.35x capex-to-revenue ratio — capital is being deployed into AI infrastructure faster than revenue can absorb it. AH dropped to $114.60 (−8.6% from $125.33 close, −49% from June ATH of $225.64). The structural question: does AI segment revenue trajectory converge toward justifying the capex burn by Q3 (reporting November), or does each quarter of elevated capex without proportional revenue acceleration further compress the stock? December 2026 lock-up expiry adds supply overhang.
trade_setups.entry: $225.64 June IPO high; $125.33 Aug 4 regular session close; $114.60 AH; $100 as psychological −56% from IPO high.
trade_setups.invalidation: Q3 AI segment revenue above $5B (vs $2.6B Q2) or Starlink reaching operating profitability breaks the capex-concern narrative upward.
trade_setups.horizon: Q3 earnings (November 2026) is the next quantitative test

bear_case: AMD delivered $6.7B in data-center revenue (+107% YoY), a beat on consensus, and a Q3 guide of $13B — and the stock sold off 8% after hours. SPCX beat revenue by 12.7% — and sold off 8.6% to $114.60. The tape is not rewarding AI hardware beats; it is selling the news on infrastructure plays priced to perfection. The 30Y at 5.20% is 20bps from clearing, but oil deflation has front-loaded its contribution; NFP Friday at 91K consensus is not soft enough to close the gap in one print. An above-130K surprise restores September above 70% and sends 30Y back toward 5.28%, reversing much of the week's rate-relief trade in a single morning. PLTR at $158.81 (approximately 99x forward sales) requires 149% US commercial growth to sustain quarterly through Q3; any deceleration below 100% compresses the multiple. If SPX closes below 7,380, this read does not hold.
